Keep it true to the code: quiz_engine.py (only combat is timed, the chain), game_input.py (C, SPACE), game_magic.py (Recall Lore: a random hint from data/hints.json, never about a creature; the Wand of Probing teaches a kind), player.py (cook caps). title: How Quizzes Work

sections.heading: Every action is a quiz
paragraphs: Nothing in the dungeon is left to luck. Each action asks questions from one subject, and your answers decide what happens.
rows: Put on a ring, amulet or other accessory
Cast a spell or zap a wand
Read a scroll or a spellbook
Disarm a trap, and some hero powers

sections.heading: Worth a closer look
paragraphs: Some things in the dungeon ask a single question of their own: a copyist's desk, a surveyor's table, a brazen head, a carved lintel. Stand beside one and press D, then D again to begin. Get it right and it gives what it holds; get it wrong and the chance is gone. They give knowledge, coin, a meal or a potion, never armour.

sections.heading: Fighting builds a chain
paragraphs: Every sum you get right adds a link to your chain, and a longer chain hits harder. A wrong answer, or the clock running out, ends the chain and you strike with what you built. Miss the very first sum and the blow misses.
Press SPACE to strike at once and keep the chain you have.

sections.heading: Only fights are timed
paragraphs: The combat clock is the only clock in the game. Every other quiz waits for you, so take the time to read it. Wisdom lengthens the combat clock, and the sidebar's Clock shows how long your next fight will give you.
The sidebar's Streak counts the questions you have answered right in a row, and Math the math questions alone. A wrong answer ends a streak; running out of time does not.

sections.heading: Dances are not quizzes
paragraphs: A dance is the one kind of thing in the dungeon that is not a quiz: watch the steps, then echo them on the arrow keys in time with the beat. Each arrow lights up as its step comes, so you can dance with the sound off. Before any dance-off you can practise as often as you like, for free, and stop any time.
Deep in the old mines, someone lonely may ask you to dance, and a dance-off with him must be won.

On a stage somewhere, a band that should have stayed dead may challenge you to a dance-off. It is Simon Says: each round one of them dances a phrase, and you copy it from memory, every round one step longer and a little faster. Win a round and its leader is done for; miss it and his song gets stuck in your head, and costs you one of three strikes. Out of strikes, they laugh you off the stage, but you can come back for a rematch.

sections.heading: Recall Lore brings back a hint
paragraphs: N asks up to five trivia questions, each harder than the last, and a wrong answer ends it. Miss the first and nothing surfaces; the further you get, the deeper the hint you bring back: a piece of the dungeon's lore, picked at random. It is never about the creature in front of you, and your mind needs rest before you can recall again.
To learn a creature, study its corpse (I, with the Philosopher's Shard) or point a Wand of Probing at it. Either way you learn the ways of its kind, and its page opens in the Bestiary.

sections.heading: What a creature's page means
paragraphs: Once you know a creature, its Bestiary page and the line you see when you meet it use a few plain words:
rows: your blow lands twice as hard
a weapon of that metal lands twice as hard
your blow lands half as hard
your blow lands a quarter as hard
both at once: three times as hard, the most a blow can gain
that effect never takes hold of it
that effect lasts half again as long on it

sections.heading: One wrong answer ends the rest
paragraphs: Wearing armour, identifying, harvesting and cooking stop at the first wrong answer. Armour asks a few questions and you need every one. A wrong identify stuns you for ten turns. A failed harvest or cook uses up what you were working on.

Armour and rings ask only the first time you wear their kind. After that the kind is known by hand: every iron breastplate goes on with no quiz, whatever its plus or blessing, though a mithril one asks its own, and a stronger ring than any of its kind you have worn asks once more. Heavy armour takes turns to put on, so dress between fights: a failed quiz loses those turns too.

Harvesting is the same. Once you have studied a creature yourself (a corpse study, or the Wand of Probing) and harvested one of its kind, every other corpse of that kind is harvested with no question.

sections.heading: Press C to read the card
paragraphs: Every question belongs to a topic, and C opens that topic's card: the whole story behind its questions, so a careful reader can answer every one. In a fight the clock stops while you read, once per question.
After a wrong answer the Remember box shows the line you needed. Press C there to read the whole card.

sections.heading: Learn from your misses
paragraphs: ; opens your missed questions, each with the right answer and the card's line, and C opens the full card from there too. Every card you have met waits in the Encyclopedia's Lore Codex (B, then m). On the title screen, F3 opens Study Mode, where you can read a topic's card and practise its questions with no clock and no risk.

sections.heading: Cooking is how you grow
paragraphs: Your maximum HP grows only from meals you cook yourself: up to 5 more on each floor. The Meals line under your HP bar shows how much of this floor's growth you have cooked. Every new floor gives that much room again, with no limit across floors.

Every dish has one main use: HP, SP, MP, a stat, or a special power. The cook menu (C) has a tab for each, Left and Right move between them, and it opens on the one you need most: HP when you are hurt, SP when you are hungry, MP when your mana runs low. Each tab shows what you can cook now and what each dish does for you, then the dishes you are building toward, greyed, with the parts still missing, so you know what to hunt. The legendary feasts are marked in gold.

On a dish you are building toward, H hunts for it, and H again stops. While you hunt, what it still needs shows gold under In Sight: a creature whose harvest gives it, or the part itself lying in view, until you hold it. Hunt as many dishes as you like; a dish you cook leaves the hunt.
People are never harvested. The body of a bandit, a knight, a cultist or an elf is searched instead: H takes a little ordinary food from what the person carried, with no question.

A dish of several parts gives more than the same parts cooked one at a time, and nothing spoils, so a part saved near the top of the dungeon can go into a feast near the bottom. The Kit (K) says what each part you carry is rich in.
A rare find of the dungeon has a dish of its own, which the cook menu shows once you hold it. Cooked, it is gone for good.
A few dishes are cooked to carry: the meal goes into your pack, wrapped, to eat later or to give to someone who has been missing it.

You are what you eat. A stat dish teaches its stat one whole point. The first one you cook on each new floor is that floor's lesson, and the Lesson line under Meals shows whether it is still open. How far a dish can raise a stat depends on its tier, the depth of its deepest part: a simple dish of shallow creatures teaches a stat only so far (up to +8), and deeper creatures teach more (up to +28 from the deepest). A dish of four ingredients or more is one tier richer. Wisdom learns half as far. The cook menu shows each stat dish's limit.
Rings and amulets of the same stat do not add up: only the strongest one counts. Wear different ones, or cook the stat you want.
